covers.title: The Hound That Would Not Bark
covers.prompt: The dry green of the invented village of Brent on a still morning in late May, a low stone sheep yard wall behind, hard sun and pale dust in the air. Close in on one boy, alone in the frame, filling most of it, camera level with his face, three-quarter view from the chest up. He is eleven, stocky, with a crop of straight brown hair and a scatter of freckles across his nose, and a solemn closed mouth that has just understood something. His smock is a faded workaday BLUE, not navy, not grey, patched at one elbow in rough orange thread, and the sleeves are rolled above the wrist. Held against his chest in both hands is one lean black and white sheepdog, the only other subject in the picture: her ears are up, her chin is lifted, and she is looking past his shoulder at the lane. Middle distance: a chalk-marked gate post, nettles, one oak in leaf. Warm morning light on his face and on the dog's white ruff, everything else in a cold blue shade. Style: painterly storybook oil, soft brushwork, canvas texture, long soft shadows. Palette: oak brown, oat, lichen green, one bright blue smock, one orange patch. Not a flat cartoon. The lane runs away behind her shoulder into flat green pasture and one low barn roof, drawn soft. Grass stems and chalk dust catch the light along the bottom edge. The boy's hands are rough and small against the dog's ribs, and the dog is heavy in them.

covers.title: The Cradle That Would Not Be Rocked
covers.prompt: A low front parlour in a farmhouse at Tolby, a village on the edge of a shallow beck, late evening in March, lamplight low and yellow and the window shuttered against the dark. Close in on one old woman, alone, filling most of the frame, camera level with her face, three-quarter view from the chest up. She is seventy-eight, with thin white hair pinned flat and a lined face, and she is looking down and to one side at something below the frame. Her shawl is PLUM, not grey, not navy, worn over a faded BLACK wool dress, the plum bright against the brown room and the cold window. She has been standing like that a good while, and her mouth is set, and she has not once put her hand out of sight. One countable anchor object stands alone in the foreground: a single white-painted wooden cradle, its rail worn pale in one place where a small hand has gripped it again and again. The hearth behind her is laid and not lit, the yard door is shut with its latch down, and the floor is bare boards with one worn track. Style: painterly storybook oil, soft brushwork, visible canvas texture, one warm lamp against a cold blue shade from the shuttered window, long soft shadows running across the floorboards. The palette runs plum, candle gold, cold slate blue, and warm grey-brown. Not a flat cartoon.

covers.title: The Boy Who Planted the Argument
covers.prompt:
Across two ploughed fields at Little Netherby a straight boundary hedge runs level to the horizon, and in one low trampled gap of it stands a young blackthorn. Late afternoon in October, the sun low and amber behind a bank of grey cloud. Behind the gap the furrows run in long parallel lines towards a farm gate and an open water hatch in the ditch.

The figure: a nine year old farm boy, alone in the frame and filling most of it, camera level with his face, three-quarter view from the waist up. Dark tousled hair, freckles across the nose, a scab on one knuckle, sleeves pushed back above grey dirt and soil under the nails. His shirt is OATMEAL, not white, not cream, and the neckerchief knotted flat at his throat is DARK GREEN, not blue, not black. He looks down at the bare ground beside his own boot, lips shut, entirely absorbed, listening to something further off than the camera.

One countable anchor object alone in the foreground: a single blackthorn cutting, glossy near the black and blunt-edged sharp, pushed upright into the turned earth at his knee, three small leaves and one tight white bud.

Style: painterly storybook oil, soft loaded brushwork, visible canvas texture, one warm light against a cold blue shade, long soft shadows falling towards the viewer.

Palette: warm ochre, oat, thorn green and amber edge light against cold slate blue and deep hedge shadow. Not a flat cartoon.

covers.title: The Candle That Burned Downward
covers.prompt: In the invented farming village of Coldbeck, on a cold blue autumn evening just after sunset, a nine-year-old girl stands on a worn stone doorstep while the first snow of the season begins to fall around her. She is alone in the frame and fills most of it, seen close in from the chest up, the camera level with her face and looking straight at her. She has dark brown hair in two short braids tied with plain wool, a round freckled face, and a steady, slightly puzzled look with her lips parted as if she has just been told something she is turning over. Her dress is SCARLET, not pink, not orange, not crimson-purple, and over it she wears a plain heather-grey wool shawl folded square at the shoulders. One object alone in the foreground: a short half-burnt candle stub standing upright on the grey flagstone step, its wax melted into a wide flat pool, its wick blackened and smoking faintly, the wax shining wet where a cloth has just wiped it clean. Behind her, softly out of focus, a low drystone wall, bare branches and the pale wash of falling snow. Style: painterly storybook oil, soft brushwork, visible canvas texture, one warm lantern-lit flame against a cold blue shade, long soft shadows raking across the step. A restrained palette of scarlet, warm amber, heather grey, snow white and cold slate blue. Not a flat cartoon.

covers.title: The Ring That Understood One Command
covers.prompt: A hedgerow lane running out beside winter ploughland in an invented rural valley called Nettlebed, at dusk on the last cold evening of March, the sky gone slate blue over bare ridges, wet grass in the wheel ruts and one bare elder along the hedge. Close in on one girl, fifteen years old, alone in the frame and filling most of it, shot at eye level with her face, chest up, three-quarter turn toward the light. She has dark hair plaited flat down her back with loose strands at her temples, a freckled sun-weathered face, and one pale eyebrow lifted. Her collarless work smock is deep madder RED, not pink, not orange, not brown, worn thin at the cuffs, and her sleeves are turned back. She holds her bare right hand up flat in front of her chin, palm to the lens, and lying alone on the open palm is one plain brass ring, sharply countable, its circle of light unmistakable. Behind her: wet grass, a bare elder, cold hills. Cold blue dusk everywhere except the last warm light on her hand and the brass. Style: painterly storybook oil, soft brushwork, canvas texture, long soft shadows. Palette: slate blue, wet green, oat, one deep red smock, one brass ring. Not a flat cartoon. The lane behind her runs away between two bare hedges to a low field wall, drawn soft, with wet stones and last year's leaves along the bottom edge. Her raised hand is the only thing held out toward the viewer, and the ring is the only bright metal in the picture.

covers.title: The Stairs That Stood One Step Higher
covers.prompt: In the single stone room of an old toll-house at a country market gate, on a grey October market morning just after the bell, one girl stands over an open ledger on a scrubbed deal table beside the door. She is close in and alone in the frame, filling most of it, camera level with her face, three-quarter view framed from the chest up, her shoulders squared and her chin tipped down as she reads. She is about thirteen, thin and serious, with straight dark brown hair cut level to her jaw and freckles dusted across her nose and cheeks. Her dress is plain SERGE, a dull oatmeal grey-brown wool, and over it she wears a knitted shawl of DEEP GREEN, a dark bottle green, not teal, not olive, not emerald. The deep green shawl reads clearly apart from the drab oatmeal serge and apart from the cold grey stone wall behind her, and a pale chalk line of a door mark runs behind her shoulder. One brass door nail lies alone in the foreground on the bare table, its flat head catching the window light. Style: painterly storybook oil, soft brushwork, visible canvas texture, one warm light from the window against a cold blue shade, long soft shadows. Palette of oat grey, bottle green, brass gold, worn timber brown and cold slate blue. Softer edges at the shoulders, clearer detail in the face and the hands. Not a flat cartoon.

covers.title: The Comb the River Gave Back
covers.prompt: A grey evening at the stone slab ford of the mill village of Tarbeck, the last daylight lying flat on slow brown river water between wet granite steps, the far bank a dark band of willows under a low overcast sky and the mill chimney just visible above the trees. Close in on one young man of twenty-six, alone in the frame and filling most of it, camera level with his face, three-quarter view from the chest up, shoulders squared to the viewer and the head tipped down. Dark brown hair wet and pushed back off his forehead, a day of work set in the jaw, clean shaven. He is wearing a heavy moleskin work coat buttoned to the throat in SCARLET, not pink, not orange, not rust, with the collar turned up and the sleeves to the wrist; the scarlet is the brightest thing in the picture. Middle distance: the wet granite steps of the ford and a slow eddy of brown water, drawn soft, and one frayed rope at the edge of the frame. Flat cold dusk everywhere except the front of the scarlet coat and the water. Style: painterly storybook oil, soft brushwork, canvas texture, long soft shadows. Palette: slate grey, wet granite, brown water, one scarlet coat. Not a flat cartoon. Water weed and wet gravel catch the last of the light along the bottom edge. His hands are large and red with cold and hang at his sides, and the scarlet wool shows a worn seam and a dark stain at one cuff.

covers.title: The Lake That Would Not Reflect the Reeve
covers.prompt:
A small invented market town on the shore of a cold northern lake, late afternoon in late October, the sun already down behind the hills and the sky flat pewter over black still water. Behind the figure the shingle runs down to three mossy washing steps and a washing line of pale sheets, all of it soft and secondary.

A girl of twelve years stands alone and close in, filling most of the frame, camera level with her face, three-quarter view from the chest up. Dark brown hair in one thick plait over her right shoulder, wind-torn, the ends still damp. Sunburnt freckled skin, a small nick on her chin, steady grey eyes looking straight out at the viewer, mouth closed and set. She wears a heavy hand-knitted shawl that is DEEP TEAL, not blue, not grey, not green, its coarse wool plainly darker and colder than the pale white of the collar showing at her throat.

In the immediate foreground, alone, she holds one wide shallow wooden bowl of still dark water in both hands, red knuckles round the rim, the rim turned up and catching the low light, the surface dead flat.

Style: painterly storybook oil, soft brushwork, visible canvas texture, one warm low light against a cold blue shade, long soft shadows.

Palette of weathered teal, iron grey, wet brown wood and pale winter skin, with one small amber highlight along the bowl rim. Not a flat cartoon.

covers.title: The Orchard Where the Promises Were Buried
covers.prompt: A bare apple orchard on the top of a hill farm at Nethergill on a cold March afternoon, four o'clock, low yellow light coming over the hedge and lying in long bars across the grass. Close in on one woman alone in the frame, filling most of it, camera level with her face, chest up, three-quarter turn toward the light. She is twenty-four, with dark hair cut blunt at the jaw and wind in it, and she wears a waxed work jacket buttoned to the throat over thick knitted sleeves, the colour MOSS GREEN, not grey, not beige, not olive, with a red jumper showing at the collar. Gloves are off. She holds both bare hands cupped together at chest height, and lying alone in her cupped hands is one russet red apple with its stem on, sharply countable against the green jacket. Behind her: six bare apple trees in rows, a hedge, long shadows across wet grass. Low yellow light on her face, her hands and the apple, everything else in a cold blue shade. Style: painterly storybook oil, soft brushwork, canvas texture, long soft shadows. Palette: oat grass, moss green, bare brown branches, one red apple. Not a flat cartoon. Six bare apple trees in rows march away behind her down the slope to a hedge and one low stone wall, drawn soft, their branches a brown scribble against the sky. Wet grass, mud and one cut branch lie along the bottom edge. Her cupped hands are the only thing in the picture held out toward the viewer, and the apple is the only bright thing in it.

covers.title: The Sleeper Who Must Be Named Exactly
covers.prompt: The small vestry room above the village church at Coldditch, on a wet Friday afternoon in late October, four o'clock light coming in low and sideways through one square window and pooling on a long varnished table, rain still running on the glass and the lane and the fen wall going grey past it. Close in and alone in the frame, filling most of it, camera level with his face, three-quarter view from the chest up: a young man of twenty-four, a parish clerk, dark hair parted flat and damp against his forehead, a narrow clean-shaven face, grey eyes held steady on something just off the lens, and a long plain work coat with the collar turned up. His coat is MOSS GREEN, not grey, not brown, not olive drab, and it is the only strong colour in the room. His sleeves are pushed back to the forearm and there is ink on the side of his right hand. In the near foreground, alone and countable, one small brass key lies on the table with its ring flat to the wood, catching the window light, well clear of everything else in the frame. Style: painterly storybook oil, soft brushwork, visible canvas texture, one warm light against a cold blue shade, long soft shadows falling across the table boards. A palette of warm ochre, brass, oxblood, wet slate and cold window blue, the room kept dim so the face carries the light. Not a flat cartoon.

covers.title: The Year the River Was Owed
covers.prompt: In the sluice house of the mill town of Tarnby, on the ninth of October at dusk, a low stone room standing over a flooded meadow where drowned hedgerow trees stand in still water, one woman bends over a long scrubbed table beside a shuttered window, the wet dark out of focus behind her. Close in on Roza Kell, forty-two, alone in the frame and filling most of it, camera level with her face, chest up. She has a broad flat weathered face, dark hair gone grey at the temples and scraped back, a small cut across one knuckle, and the tired squint of somebody who has read small figures by lamplight for eleven years. Her heavy work jacket is deep bottle GREEN, not black, not navy, and she wears a faded madder red wool scarf knotted at the collar over it. Alone in the foreground on the bare scrubbed board, standing clear of the lamp glare, one open ruled ledger with five columns, the second headed NAMES and a single inked name in it, a brass-tipped pen lying across the page. Style: painterly storybook oil, soft brushwork, visible canvas texture, one warm oil-lamp light against a cold blue window shade, long soft shadows lying across the tabletop and up the damp stone wall. Palette of bottle green, madder red, wet slate blue, lamp gold and old paper cream. Not a flat cartoon.

covers.title: The Fire That Fed on Words
covers.prompt: Hollowmere, a ring of old stones in a wet valley village, at half past five on a grey winter afternoon. Close in on a girl of sixteen, alone in the frame and filling most of it, camera level with her face, three-quarter view from the chest up. She is thin through the shoulders, her face pale and freckled across the nose, her eyebrows dark, and she is looking slightly to the left of the lens rather than straight down it. Her hair is ink-black, wet at the ends, braided over one shoulder. Her coat is SCARLET, not pink, not orange. Her hands are chapped red and she is holding one wet white sheet at chest height, mouth slightly open. In the foreground, alone and countable, a single white enamel washboard lies face up on the wet stones. Behind her the fire glows low and orange in the ring, softened by rain. The washing line runs from an iron bar driven into the stones out to a post, and beyond that a grey hedge and a leaning boundary wall go away down the valley. Style: painterly storybook oil, soft brushwork, visible canvas texture, one warm light from the fire against a cold blue shade, long soft shadows across the stones. Palette: cold slate blues and greys, wet stone and dusk, with one ember orange and one saturated scarlet as the only strong colours. Not a flat cartoon.
